note: 'you received the Spirit of adoption to sonship, by whom we cry, Abba! Father!' (Rom 8:15). The crying and the adoption are named in one clause, the second as the ground of the first.

'you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption to sonship, by whom we cry, Abba! Father!' (Rom 8:15). Fear is named as what the cry is not from. The verse defines the word by contrast, which is the only thing the corpus says about how it is meant.

'Abba, Father,” He said, “all things are possible for You.' (Mark 14:36). The three occurrences pair the word with 'Father' every time, so what it names is not in doubt. Jesus is the speaker in Mark; in Rom 8:15 and Gal 4:6 it is believers.

'the Spirit of adoption to sonship, by whom we cry, Abba! Father!' (Rom 8:15). The phrase and the cry are the same sentence; Gal 4:6 says the same thing with 'the Spirit of his Son' in place of 'the Spirit of adoption'.
